q7.answer: On confirmation, one transaction makes the pending secret active, sets last_used_step to the matched step, deletes the user's old recovery codes and inserts 10 new hashed ones, and deletes the user's other sessions while keeping the current sid. If any part fails, the whole transaction rolls back, so the state stays SetupPending or ReplacementPending, the old codes and sessions remain, and nothing is partly applied.

q8.answer: The 'password OK, code still needed' state is a server-side login_challenges row (token_hash, user_id, expires_at, wrong_attempts). The browser holds only the raw challenge token in its own short-lived cookie, separate from sid. The row is deleted on success, on the 5th wrong entry, and on expiry (checked on any request after 5 minutes).

q9.answer: The authenticator secrets live sealed with seal() in totp_factors.active_secret_sealed and totp_factors.pending_secret_sealed. Enrolment status is read from which of those columns are set (pending only means SetupPending, active only means On, both means ReplacementPending). Replay protection is totp_factors.last_used_step. Recovery codes are sha256 hashes in recovery_codes with used_at. 2FA counts as on when active_secret_sealed is set, and a pending secret alone does not turn it on.

q10.answer: Sign-in reads only active_secret_sealed, so while a replacement is pending the old authenticator keeps working and the new pending secret does nothing until confirmed. I did not decide what happens when the user abandons a replacement: no cancel transition or pending-secret expiry is drawn, so the pending secret would simply stay stored and ignored until the user starts setup again, which overwrites it. That cleanup is unspecified.

q11.answer: I did not specify how the second step tells an authenticator code from a recovery code; the document only says it checks the entry against a valid TOTP and against an unused recovery code, with no format rule. Wrong recovery codes do count: any entry the server does not accept during a challenge, including a recovery code, adds 1 to wrong_attempts, and the same 5-entry limit applies to both kinds.
